# v2.64 Release Notes

This stable release rolls up dev pre-releases **v2.61-dev … v2.64-dev**. It focuses
on the **Compliance Planning** "Who to certify" experience — a full candidate pool,
clearer explanations, matching exports, and a double-counting fix.

## New: see every eligible candidate, not just the recommended few

The roadmap tells you a requirement has, say, "24 easy" candidates, but "Who to
certify" only lists the cheapest subset the plan nominates. A new **"All eligible
candidates"** section now appears below it, listing the **full pool** — everyone who
already holds qualifying training and could be certified, deduped across the whole
plan. Same columns, drill-down, sorting and CSV/Excel/PDF export, and it's included
in the whole-page Export report. Use it to pick alternatives when the cheapest
recommended person isn't the one you want to move.

## Improved: plain-language explanations in "Who to certify" (and exports)

Expanding a person now spells out each gap in plain language, worded to match their
situation:

- **Easy win** — "They have taken *Training A*. Passing the *Cert A* certification
  exam will contribute to the *Specialisation Y* specialisation."
- **Lapsed** — "They previously held *Cert A*, but it has expired. Renewing it will
  contribute to the *Specialisation Y* specialisation."
- **Legacy upgrade** — "They hold the legacy certification *Cert B*. Upgrading to
  *Cert A* will contribute to the *Specialisation Y* specialisation."

The exported report's **Detail** column now uses the same wording (previously a
terse internal format), so the file matches what's on screen — one sentence per gap.

## Fixed: double-counted gaps when a certification is shared across specialisations

When one certification satisfied more than one specialisation you selected, the plan
double-counted it — a person could show the **same gap twice** (an inflated "Gaps
closed"), and each shared gap's fill was counted twice, making the plan
**under-count net-new** and **nominate fewer candidates than the gap actually
needs**. The allocator now credits each person to a requirement at most once, so the
drill-down, "People to certify", "Net-new training", and the candidate list are all
accurate. If you plan against a shared certification, expect these figures to move —
they were under-counting before.

## Notes

- No database migration and no configuration changes.
